Contractor shall provide correction curves for gross power output of the Steam turbine versus ambient conditions of dry bulb temperature and relative humidity. The orientation and layout of the ACC shall be such that the adequate air circulation is possible around the ACC.
Each ACC fan shall be individually isolatable. Access ways, galleries, platforms and ladders shall be provided for safe and efficient operation and maintenance including maintenance of fans, gearboxes, bearings etc. The ACC shall comprise a number of cells mounted on a hot dip galvanised steel support structure. Lockable access doors shall be provided in the partition walls (normally kept closed and locked).

The ACC shall be designed for full vacuum to an approved heat exchanger design code as applicable such as Heat Exchanger Institute (HEI) Standards for Steam Surface Condensers, ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code etc.
The ACC shall be of the forced draught type, located on a steel structure at ground level. It shall be capable of condensing steam from the steam turbine and turbine drain flash vessel (if provided) at all ambient conditions and at all loads.
The ACC shall be arranged to minimise the recirculation of cooling air.
During steam turbine trip transient/start-up phase, the whole steam flow from the by-pass system will be discharged to the ACC.
During the by-pass conditions, the ACC shall be able to maintain the pressure such that no limitation occurs for the steam turbine capabilities.
In addition to the requirements of Exhibit B, Part 1; the ACC shall be designed to be capable of condensing the entire steam flow dumped by the by pass system following a steam turbine trip, for indefinite time.

Wind walls shall be installed around the perimeter of the ACC structure, minimally extending from fan deck level to the top of the heat exchanger bundles. Each ACC shall be equipped with systems such as high pressure spray to enable cleaning of the outer surfaces of the tubes.

Chunk Text:
An integrated structure carrying the condenser, fans and motors, plenum chamber, access galleries, staircases, platforms and maintenance runway beams shall be supplied and secured to ground foundation concrete supports. Steelwork, platforms, ladders and stairways shall be hot dip galvanized.
The height of the structure shall take account of the air velocity when operating with all fans in service. The ACC shall be designed with a fan deck at least 16m high to minimize air recirculation.
The structural steelwork shall be capable of supporting the ACC at all operating, maintenance and testing loads and shall comply with the wind speed design loadings given for the Site. Where stress analysis calculations are performed, the location of anchors, guides or restraints shall be based on the results of the final stress analysis. Such anchors, guides and restraints shall be designed for the maximum forces and moments encountered.
The civil engineering and structural works shall be designed in accordance with accepted codes and standards of skill, care and diligence.
The seismic design, both for structural sizing and operating behavior, shall comply with the minimum seismic requirements provided in Exhibit B, Part 1.
The design, fabrication, testing, installation and fixing method of all steelwork including structural members, checker plate flooring, handrailing, ladders, open grid flooring and stair treads shall be in accordance with recognized codes and standards for steelwork.
The necessary signalizations shall be foreseen.
Stairs shall be preferred to ladders wherever possible. Where ladders are used they shall be installed only in areas where only occasional access is required or where space limitations so dictate.

Keywords: condensate return from ACCs, condensate return from FGP, CPP treated condensate, deaerator/feedwater tanks, water/steam cycle balancing, FGP return condensate temperature <100°C, cooling prior to CPP, Fin Fan Cooler, N+2 modules, module isolation without impacting full condensate flow, CPP inlet temperature requirement 60°C at design conditions, condensate storage tank flashing at atmospheric pressure, condensate storage connection before/after CPP away from normal path
Chunk Text:
Refer to Exhibit B -Part 1.
The condensate system includes return from the ACCs and also from the FGP. Condensate return from the ACCs shall mix with FGP return condensate which has been treated in the CPP. The final condensate shall be directed to the deaerator/feedwater tanks (with consideration of balancing the water in each water/steam cycle if necessary).
FGP return condensate is at high temperature (<100°C) and must be cooled prior to entering the CPP. A Fin Fan Cooler shall be considered with N+2 modules where any one module can be isolated for repair without impacting the full condensate flow. The fin fan cooler shall be designed to meet CPP inlet temperature requirements of 60 °Cat design conditions.
Because the FGP condensate return temperature is <100°C, it is not possible to consider the condensate storage tank as part of the normal operating cycle as the water will flash if it goes to atmospheric pressure. Condensate storage tank should therefore be connected either before or after the CPP where the condensate temperature is low. Additionally; condensate storage should be connected away from the normal path of the condensate.
The condensate coming from the ACC and from the condensate polishing system shall be directed to the deaerator/feedwater tanks (with consideration of balancing the water in each water/steam cycle if necessary).

- Lube oil heater for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Power Plant Jockey pumps : 2x100%
- Heat exchangers (not applicable to fin fan cooler or to air cooled condenser). Redundancy should be considered to eliminate single point of failure that will result in reduced load.

- Tanks (if not mentioned hereunder) : more than 1
- CCW Expansion Tanks : 1 x 100%
- Atmospheric drain tank : 1 x 100%
- Vacuum Flash Tank : 1 x 100%
- Condensate Storage Tank : 2x50% or 1x100%
- Service air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- Instrument air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- H2 Tanks : 2 x 50%
- Diesel storage tank : 2 x 50%
- Gas Drain Collection Tank (GT Area) : 1 x 100%
- GT Fuel Gas Last Chance Filter (per GT) : 2 x 100% Chemical tanks
- DM plant : N+1 stream
- Air conditioning :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house)
- Ventilation Fans :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house))
- Gas reducing station : 3 x 50%
- Feed water control stations : 2 x 100%
- Fuel Gas Boosting Compressors: : N+1, where, N=Number of Gas Turbines
- Air  compressors  with  after  coolers  (after  coolers  if  required,  will  be  confirmed  during  detail engineering) : 3x50%
- Air filtering skids : 2 x 100%
- Air dryers : 2 x 100%
- After Filters : 2 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each GT : 1 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each ST : 1 x 100%
- N2 rack & manifold station : 1 x 100%
- H2 generator : 2 x 100%
- Drain and vent valves :  two  valves  in  series  (If  operating  pressure  is greater than 4 MPa) otherwise single valve
- Level control valve for HRSG Drums and Feedwater tank :  N+1 (not applicable for startup line, as applicable)

Chunk Text:
Air cooled condenser(s) will be required to let down steam from the condensing part of the steam turbine and from the LP-steam headers.
The system shall comprise at least the following equipment:
- steam duct from the steam reducing stations to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- steam duct from turbine exhaust flange to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- condensate collection headers,
- air moving system,
- fan drives,
- steel support structure, including maintenance platforms, access stairways and escape ladder,
- facilities for prevention of air recirculation,
- noise attenuation features/devices as required,
- all  required  electrical  and  control  equipment  for  safe  operation,  monitoring  and  measuring, earthing and lightning protection,
- air evacuation pumps, if applicable,
- ejector condenser, drain tank and strainers at ejector steam inlets,
- condensate tank and drain,
- drain and vent pumping, piping, valves and traps with supports, and
- semi-automatic ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning system.
The steam turbine condenser shall be complete in every respect for reliable, efficient and safe operation for a high service lifetime. The design of the air-cooled condenser shall be in accordance with the ambient conditions at Project Site and steam turbine requirements.
The condenser shall be sized to receive:
- Condense all steam for all operating ranges
- Accept the full steam turbine bypass steam when the steam turbine trips.
The  capacity  of  the  steam  turbine  condenser  shall  include  a  reserve  to  cover  possible  steam  turbine overloads.

Keywords: air cooled condenser (ACC), steam turbine exhaust to condenser steam duct, LP-steam headers letdown, condensate collection headers, air moving system, fan drives, steel support structure (platforms, stairways, escape ladder), air recirculation prevention, noise attenuation features, earthing and lightning protection, air evacuation pumps, ejector condenser drain tank strainers, condensate tank and drain, drain and vent pumping (valves, traps), steam turbine bypass steam on trip, reserve capacity for steam turbine overloads, ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning (semi-automatic)
Chunk Text:
Air cooled condenser(s) will be required to let down steam from the condensing part of the steam turbine and from the LP-steam headers.
The system shall comprise at least the following equipment:
- steam duct from the steam reducing stations to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- steam duct from turbine exhaust flange to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- condensate collection headers,
- air moving system,
- fan drives,
- steel support structure, including maintenance platforms, access stairways and escape ladder,
- facilities for prevention of air recirculation,
- noise attenuation features/devices as required,
- all  required  electrical  and  control  equipment  for  safe  operation,  monitoring  and  measuring, earthing and lightning protection,
- air evacuation pumps, if applicable,
- ejector condenser, drain tank and strainers at ejector steam inlets,
- condensate tank and drain,
- drain and vent pumping, piping, valves and traps with supports, and
- semi-automatic ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning system.
The steam turbine condenser shall be complete in every respect for reliable, efficient and safe operation for a high service lifetime. The design of the air-cooled condenser shall be in accordance with the ambient conditions at Project Site and steam turbine requirements.
The condenser shall be sized to receive:
- Condense all steam for all operating ranges
- Accept the full steam turbine bypass steam when the steam turbine trips.
The  capacity  of  the  steam  turbine  condenser  shall  include  a  reserve  to  cover  possible  steam  turbine overloads.
